findings.evidence: Measured both builds in a scratch copy with identical rollup/plugins: HEAD (v1.7.0) dist/index.js = 122706 bytes, dist/index.esm.js = 122244; working tree = 123360 and 122892 (+654 and +648 bytes). The growth comes from the added off-state reset effect/comment (lines 338-344) and the MenuButton helper (lines 42-43). No test measures build output: searching all *.test.* for dist/index, bundle, gzip or size-limit finds nothing and there is no .size-limit.json, so nothing would fail if the bundle grew further.
findings.description: The performance non-functional requirement ("npm run build output for dist/index.js and dist/index.esm.js is no larger than v1.7.0's (measure both before and after)") is both unmet and unproven: both bundles are measurably larger than v1.7.0's and no test/measurement enforces the limit (TEST-001 is also unmet for this requirement).

findings.evidence: The R2 tests cover placeholder, filtering, clearing, autofocus, rail, empty state and numbered shortcuts, but no test passes searchIcon or asserts a custom icon renders (grep for searchIcon in every *.test.* file returns no matches).
findings.description: R2 names searchIcon among the 1.7.0 behaviours that must keep working; no test would fail if the searchIcon prop stopped being honoured.

findings.evidence: The default-props accessibility test asserts only that there is no textbox and that document.activeElement is not an HTMLInputElement; no test drives Tab, ArrowDown, Escape or Digit keys with default props to show focus never lands on a hidden control, and no test reaches the opt-in input by keyboard (only the searchAutoFocus programmatic focus is asserted at line 415).
findings.description: The accessibility non-functional requirement's keyboard-traversal acceptance is only partly proven; the unmounted input makes the hidden case structurally safe, but the claim is not asserted.

findings.evidence: The R3 test asserts the version, the migration snippet, the already-passing-false sentence and the no-export sentence, but no assertion covers the note's opening claim "Search itself is otherwise unchanged" (docs/breaking-changes.md:73), which R3's edge case requires the note to state.
findings.description: One R3 edge case (the note says search is otherwise unchanged) is present in the document but not covered by any test assertion.

findings.evidence: The prev/next links are asserted only for docs/api.md and docs/configuration.md (lines 831-832 and 841-842); features.md, examples.md, breaking-changes.md and README still have their links but a dropped link would not fail. The docs scan checks six files and only two phrasings, so a contradiction in docs/best-practices.md or docs/development.md, or one worded differently, would not be caught. The README feature-list wording ("Search is off by default") is also not asserted, only that searchEnabled={true} appears somewhere in README.
findings.description: R4's page-by-page guarantees are only partially asserted; the docs are currently correct but the tests would not notice several regressions.

findings.evidence: npx jest gives 214 passed / 2 failed. Both failures (lines 180 and 219) are the pre-existing Windows CRLF regex mismatches in the untouched Styles/SidekickMenu.theme.test.ts; every search test passes and none is deleted or skipped.
findings.description: R5's "npm test passes" is literally unmet because of the pre-existing, unrelated CRLF failures; the search-specific part of R5 is satisfied.

findings.evidence: There is no scripts/consumer-smoke.mjs and no other install/import check, so the packed library was not installed into a scratch project or imported under CommonJS and ES modules. npm pack --dry-run shows files:["dist"] only (62 files, 600.8 kB, including dist/**/*.test.d.ts).
findings.description: The packed-library install/import half of LIB-003 is not exercised by this project; this is pre-existing project state, not introduced by the change.
